findings.claim: the arm JSON line 178 records scratch_scope_run_rows 0 while scratch_family_rows is 50 in the same graph
findings.text: follow-on: the containment paragraph cites the run-id arm of the negative control as corroborating evidence ('The negative control saw 0 rows attributable to this apply on the live graph, by family members and by run id alike'), but that arm has no discriminating power. The same probe reads 0 on the scratch copy the apply demonstrably wrote to: the arm record carries scratch_scope_run_rows 0 at docs/evidence/fragments/sn-selection-over-generation/ssog-anchor-ab/current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport-jev.json:178, while the family-rows probe on the same scratch graph found 50 rows. A probe that returns 0 where 50 rows are known to exist measures nothing, so its 0 on the live graph cannot corroborate containment, and the sentence presents a vacuous half as if it were a second control. The verdict still holds on the family-rows arm, which does discriminate (50 on scratch, 0 on live), so this does not block the node; it is a defect of the runner's containment instrument reproduced in this node's evidence chain, and it is shared by every sibling arm record.

findings.claim: isolation.at 21:20:42 precedes the row counts it carries, which were measured at 21:50:47
findings.text: follow-on: the isolation block's 'at' is the pre-apply isolation-proof timestamp 2026-10-19T21:20:42.936699+00:00, but the same block also carries the post-apply row counts the containment check measured at 21:50:47 (scratch_family_rows 50, scratch_ledger_rows 50, live_family_rows 0). The runner merges those measurements into the isolation dict after the apply ('data["isolation"].update(...)' at ssog-anchor-ab-run.py:607), leaving the earlier 'at' in place, so a reader who takes the block's timestamp as the time of its contents reads 50 family cost rows as existing before the apply started at 21:20:50. No numeric claim in the record is wrong and the containment block carries its own correct 'at', so this does not block; it is a runner-produced misattribution shared by every sibling arm record.
